changes.before: Implement renameNote(notes,id,title). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Rename the matching note in a new array while preserving the original.

before: An immutable update returns a new collection while leaving the caller’s existing collection unchanged. Only the matching record receives the new title.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
map creates a new array. For the matching ID, {...note,title} copies the record and replaces its title. Unmatched records are reused because this function does not mutate them.

Read the function call renameNote([{"id":1,"title":"Moon"},{"id":2,"title":"Sea"}], 2, "Ocean") from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, renameNote runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
Why test with ordinary mutable input as well as frozen input? An accidental write can fail silently on frozen objects. Comparing mutable input before and after catches a real change.
after: An immutable update returns a new result without editing the caller's original data. Here, the result keeps every note in order and changes only the title for the requested ID.
map builds a new array by choosing a result for each item. Compare note.id with the requested id to decide which note needs the new title.

{...note, title} copies the matching note's fields, then replaces title in that copy. Unmatched notes can be reused because this function does not edit them. A missing ID leaves all note values unchanged in the new array.

Check the original data after the function runs. Also test with ordinary changeable objects: an attempted write to a frozen object may fail silently in some JavaScript code. Frozen means the object's own properties have been locked against changes.
Complete renameNote(notes, id, title). Match the ID exactly, copy the matching record with the new title, and return all others unchanged. Do not write to a note from the input array.

before.question: Why test with ordinary mutable input as well as frozen input?
choices: Frozen input proves every side effect
Mutable input lets the test observe accidental writes directly
before.explanation: An accidental write can fail silently on frozen objects. Comparing mutable input before and after catches a real change.

after.question: Why also test with ordinary changeable input instead of only frozen objects?
choices: Frozen objects reveal every possible side effect
The test can directly observe an accidental change
after.explanation: An attempted write may fail silently on a frozen object. Changeable input lets the test spot a real unwanted change.

project.title: Replace one record without changing the input
project.task: Complete renameNote(notes, id, title) with a new array and a copied matching note. Preserve all other fields and the original input.
project.done_when: Only the matching title changes in the result, and the input remains unchanged.
